explanation: The Punchbowl article opens its prelude with where the front came to rest: "The Chinese People's Volunteer Army (PVA) Spring Offensive was stopped by 20 May 1951 and UN forces counterattacked forcing the PVA back to Line Kansas along the southern edge of the Punchbowl by 20 June." The two armies fought from that line three months later, so the offensive's failure is what put them on the rim of the Punchbowl at all. The type is `precondition-of` because the article gives the ground, and attributes the decision to attack it to the breakdown of the armistice talks in August. The confidence is `probable` because Wikipedia is the only source.
